system: Gynodioecious populations in alpine southwestern China, female and hermaphrodite flowers

primary_studies.title: A sexually dimorphic corolla appendage affects pollen removal and floral longevity in gynodioecious Cyananthus delavayi (Campanulaceae)
primary_studies.access: Full-text public PLOS ONE; PMC abstract/results indexed, current web view intermittently blocked by bot check

observed.reduced_pollen_removal: Male phase prolonged at female phase's expense
observed.no_pollen_removal: Approximately one-third of hermaphroditic flowers never reached a female phase under the two no-removal procedures
observed.throat_hair_excision: Increased pollen removal per halictid bee visit and shortened male phase
observed.biological_ceiling: Pollen-phase trade-off observed, but no experimentally established historical origin and no direct paternal reproductive success

primary_studies.author_figure2_label: NHR netted/no hair removal; HR hair removal; C natural control; 0%, 50%, 100% pollen removal are distinct pollinator-excluded manipulations

primary_studies.title: Evaluation of pollinator effectiveness based on pollen deposition and seed production in a gynodieocious alpine plant, Cyananthus delavayi

sampling.site: Shangri-La Alpine Botanical Garden, Yunnan, SW China

measured: Pollen grains on stigmas 8-10 h after a single visit
Seed number in fruits collected after 30 days

observed.hoverfly: Single visits produced fewer seeds than bumblebee or halictid bee visits
observed.visit_pollen_vs_seed: Stigma pollen count failed to explain seed number in published fitted model while pollinator group did
observed.limit: Failed to reject an association is not proof of zero pollen effect; pollen origin and compatibility unknown

primary_studies.title: Sexual conflict in protandrous flowers and the evolution of gynodioecy
primary_studies.access: Publisher abstract and publisher-listed supporting information descriptions; original full article behind paywall, raw experimental data not obtained
primary_studies.locations: Five reported field populations near Shangri-La City, SW China
primary_studies.intervention: Experimental early versus restricted pollen removal from protandrous hermaphroditic flowers

published_results.early_removal: Hermaphrodite seed production became similar to female seed production
published_results.restricted_removal: Male phase extended, female phase shortened and hermaphrodite female fertility lowered
published_results.female_advantage_across_five_populations: Approximately 2-fold seed fertility advantage on average
published_results.reported_scope: Sex-specific fitness advantage and phase competition are published findings, not reestimated here

primary_studies.inference_boundary: Supports current floral sexual interference and a conditional ecological route favoring females, not a measured allele invasion/fixation or identified historical origin of gynodioecy

comparative_interpretation.complementary_wurmbea_2004: Wurmbea pollinator-exclusion sign varies among sex morphs, and pollen metering differs; Cyananthus pollen-removal directly manipulates temporal male/female phase competition and maternal seed output
comparative_interpretation.common_positive: Reproductive opportunity has separate sex-specific temporal and seed-maturation stages
comparative_interpretation.different_causal_treatments: Whole-plant pollinator exclusion is NOT equivalent to flower-level experimental pollen removal

interpretation_limits: 2015 and 2021 studies involve the same plant species and overlapping author network; do not count as two independent evolutionary transitions
2017 measures pollen and seed from the same single-visit experimental flower, but this is not the 2021 pollen-removal treatment cohort
5 populations in 2021 refer to reported female seed advantage; avoid assuming 5 independent populations for every specific intervention without full Methods
2021 accessible source is abstract/supplementary listing only; do not claim source-verified exact effect sizes, CIs or treatment sample sizes
2017 conditional F and p are author-reported fitted-model statistics, not new regressions, causal mediation or null-effect proof
2015 0% pollen removal trials can suppress female phase without showing historical fixation or heritable disappearance of female genetic capacity
No direct comparison with Wurmbea at matched pollinator guild, floral phases, geography, units or genetic backgrounds
Experiments reveal contemporary function and constraints, not taxon-specific histories of sexual-system evolution
Do not imply any included study was conducted by SLK authors
